title: Customer communication, warranty, access and privacy on appliance jobs
referencesAtStart: Official references for this lesson: ACCC, Consumer rights and guarantees (business) (no date in page body; page metadata shows published and modified 2026-07-17); OAIC, Privacy for small business (no date in page body; page metadata shows published 2023-03-10).
audience: Workers and supervisors who speak with owners, operators and site contacts about appliance cleaning, scope, warranty, access and photographs
learningOutcomes: Confirm the customer's authority, access and the state of the appliance before the job starts
Explain the limits of the cleaning service without promising repair, safety or warranty outcomes
Handle warranty and damage questions by recording facts and referring them to the right person
Take and store job photographs in a way that respects the customer's privacy and confidential information

instruction.heading: Confirm authority, access and the appliance's state before you start
instruction.body: The first conversation on the job sets the terms. Confirm the name of the person who has authority to approve the work, the site contact for the day, the access arrangements, the parking, the times when the kitchen or workshop is available, and whether the appliance is in service. Ask whether the machine has been used recently, whether it still holds oil or hot water, and whether any fault has been reported. If the machine is in use, ask the owner to shut it down under the site procedure, and make sure the owner understands that you will not operate it. Confirm that the cleaning is the job that was booked, and tell the contact about any part of the scope that you cannot clean under this course. Record each confirmation with the time and the person's name, because these facts protect the customer, the worker and the business if a question comes up later.

instruction.heading: Explain the limits without promising a result
instruction.body: Customers often expect a cleaner to make an appliance look new, work better, or be free of faults. Explain what the job can and cannot do. You can say that the exterior and accessible parts will be cleaned to the agreed standard, and that internal parts, electrical parts, gas parts and refrigeration parts are not part of the service. You should not say that a machine is safe, will work properly, or will pass an inspection, because you cannot know that from cleaning alone. You should not say that cleaning will restore a finish that has worn away, or that a stain will come out without testing. If the customer asks for a repair or an adjustment, tell them who can do it and that the business will refer the job. Keep the tone plain and honest, and avoid technical jargon that suggests you have more authority than you do.

instruction.heading: Warranty, damage claims and photographs
instruction.body: Warranty terms are set by the manufacturer and are often conditional on how the appliance is cleaned, serviced and used. Consumer guarantees are separate: they apply automatically and a warranty cannot remove them. If a customer asks whether the clean will affect the warranty, do not answer from memory. Say that the manufacturer's warranty sits on top of the consumer guarantees, and record the question. If you find a fault or damage before you clean, photograph it with the appliance in view and record it, so that it is not blamed on the clean. If damage occurs during the job, stop, make the item safe, photograph it, and report it to the supervisor the same day. Do not admit liability on site, and do not promise compensation. Photographs of the appliance are normally taken to show the condition before and after the clean. Take only the photographs that the job needs. Do not photograph people, screens showing customer information, paperwork, staff rosters, security codes or private areas. Store job photographs in the business system only, and remove them from personal devices in line with the business's privacy procedure. Whether the Privacy Act binds the business depends on turnover and activity: businesses with turnover at or under $3 million are generally outside it unless an exception applies.

procedure: Before the job, confirm the name of the person who approves the work, the site contact for the day and the access arrangements.
On arrival, confirm whether the appliance is in service, whether it holds oil or hot water, and whether a fault has been reported.
Ask for the appliance to be shut down under the site procedure, and confirm you will not operate it.
Explain the scope in plain words, including the parts you will not clean and the referral route for them.
Photograph the existing condition of each appliance with its data plate in shot, and record any pre-existing fault.
If a customer asks about warranty, record the question, say that the manufacturer's warranty sits on top of the consumer guarantees, and refer it to the supervisor.
If damage occurs during the job, make the item safe, photograph it, and report it to the supervisor the same day without admitting liability.
Before you leave, confirm the outcome with the site contact, and record the names, times and any open questions.

workedExamples.situation: A customer says the commercial oven has been cleaned by you before and the warranty was kept, and asks you to confirm in writing that the clean will not affect the warranty.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What do you say and do?
workedExamples.reasoning: Say that the manufacturer's warranty sits on top of the consumer guarantees, record the request, and tell the supervisor so the business can respond in writing. Do not promise that the clean will not affect the warranty, and do not write a statement that the business cannot verify.

workedExamples.situation: While cleaning a fryer's exterior, you accidentally knock the edge of the control panel and a small plastic strip lifts away. The site contact is in the kitchen.
workedExamples.reasoning: Stop the job at that part, make the area safe, and photograph the strip and its position. Tell the site contact plainly what happened, without blaming anyone and without promising a cost. Report it to the supervisor the same day, and record the time and the people who were told. Do not try to re-fix the strip with adhesive or tape, because that is a repair.

equipmentAndPpe: Job record on a device, with the site contact and the access notes
Business camera or device for photographs, set to store job images in the business system
Customer-facing script or card with the scope and referral route, as provided by the business

commonErrors.error: Telling the customer that the appliance is safe or fully working after a clean.
commonErrors.prevention: Describe what was cleaned and what was not. Do not give safety or working assurances from cleaning alone.

commonErrors.error: Answering a warranty question from memory.
commonErrors.prevention: Say the warranty sits on top of the consumer guarantees, record the question and refer it to the supervisor.

commonErrors.error: Photographing screens, paperwork or people, or keeping job photos on a personal device.
commonErrors.prevention: Photograph only the appliance and its condition, and store images in the business system only.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Information about customers, premises and staff is personal or confidential. Photographs and notes must be limited to what the job needs and stored under the business privacy procedure.
Consumer guarantees sit alongside those conditions. The business must not give a warranty opinion.
This lesson does not grant a licence or authority to give safety certification, to inspect regulated installations, or to carry out any regulated appliance work.

qualityStandard: The approver, site contact, access and appliance state are confirmed and recorded before work starts
The scope limits are explained in plain words, and no safety, working or warranty assurance is given
Photographs are limited to the appliance and its condition, and are stored in the business system
documentationEvidence: The name, role and time of each person who confirmed the scope and access
Before photographs of each appliance with its data plate, and any pre-existing fault recorded
Any warranty question, damage report or complaint, with the referral made and the time
summary: Confirm who approves the work, the access, and whether the appliance is in service before you start.
Explain what the clean covers and what it does not, without promising safety, function or warranty outcomes.
Photograph the appliance only, record damage and questions, and refer warranty and liability matters to the supervisor.

knowledgeChecks.question: A customer asks whether cleaning will keep the manufacturer's warranty valid. What is the correct response?
options: Say that the manufacturer's warranty sits on top of the consumer guarantees, record the question, and refer it to the supervisor
Confirm that the warranty is always kept after a clean, since cleaning never affects any manufacturer terms or conditions at all
Say the warranty is void for every clean, so the customer should not book any cleaning service at all in the future
Give the warranty number from memory, along with the full terms that the manufacturer printed on the card last year

knowledgeChecks.question: Which statement after a clean is accurate and within this course?
options: The machine is now safe and will pass any inspection by the authority or the manufacturer, with nothing else needed
The exterior and accessible parts were cleaned to the agreed standard, and internal and electrical parts were not part of the service
The fault in the control panel has been fixed and tested, so the appliance is now working as the manufacturer intended
The gas burner is clean and ready to use, with its flame settings checked and the gas supply confirmed safe for the customer

knowledgeChecks.question: Which photograph is appropriate for a job record?
options: A photograph of the staff roster on the wall, showing the names of the crew
A photograph of a customer's paperwork on the bench, so the details can be checked
A photograph of the appliance and its data plate showing its existing condition
A photograph of a security code keypad, taken from the front to show the layout

knowledgeChecks.question: During a clean, a plastic strip on a control panel lifts away. What is the first step?
options: Stick it back with strong adhesive before anyone notices the damage on the panel
Admit full liability and offer the customer a refund on site, to settle the matter quickly
Continue the clean and mention it on the invoice, so the customer knows about the strip
Stop at that part, make the area safe, photograph it, and tell the site contact and supervisor

knowledgeChecks.question: Why should you confirm whether an appliance is in service before cleaning?
options: Because a machine in use may hold oil, hot water or live parts, and it must be shut down under the site procedure
So the customer can watch the clean from the doorway and check that the method looks right to them
Because all appliances must be switched on for cleaning, so the crew can test the controls at the start
Because the customer must pay before cleaning begins, and payment confirms that the machine is in service
